New compared to the original: cultural borders (no founding a city in foreign territory, at least 4 tiles between cities; the space between neighboring cities of the same wizard, up to 10 tiles, belongs to them), automatic allocation of farmers to feed the armies, the city list that comes back after you consult it, automatic battles at any time.

The Veil (indicator at the top) wears down with time, crossings between planes and major spells; at each threshold, rifts open: they serve as passages between Arcanus and Myrror, but creatures come out of them. Shrines (two on Arcanus, four on Myrror) offer a pact: a gift right away, a debt later. The Crisis (adjustable at game creation) opens the Breach, which sends waves against the most powerful wizard until it is closed.

Combat terrain (hover over a tile for its effects): trees cover from missiles (+2 defense) but burn, and fire spreads; a hill gives +10% to hit at range and +1 defense in melee; rocks block the way; the deep water of a river can only be crossed by swimming, by flying or at one of the two fords, which cost all movement and leave you exposed (-1 defense); swamp bogs mire units.

Accuracy: at 100%, every hit lands; beyond that, each 10% bracket ignores 1 point of the target's defense (not the wall's).

Dilemmas: every 8 to 12 turns, a situation to settle, with two outcomes whose consequences are spelled out. Nemeses: whoever slays one of your heroes receives a name, grows stronger (+1 per rank to attack, defense and resistance) and may come back for you; slaying it in turn yields gold, Fame and experience.

Diplomacy: the wizards screen details what shapes each wizard's attitude toward you (treaties, attacks, borders, magic realms, common enemy…). A far stronger wizard may demand gold or a spell; if they issue an ultimatum, refusing means war. Spells can be traded between wizards who can learn them. A wizard of honor denounces a treaty six turns before being able to attack; only a treacherous one breaks it without warning. A war that costs too much makes peace easier to obtain.

Race for Mastery: who is studying or casting the Spell of Mastery, and in how many turns, is known to all (indicator at the top). Whoever casts it draws the war of every wizard; taking their Fortress stops it. Overextended empire: a city more than 20 tiles from the Fortress, or on the other plane, has one more rebel; from 20 cities on, all of them (except the Fortress) have one more.

Flank and rear: the chevron on the ground shows where the unit is facing (its last step, its last target; when struck, it turns around). Striking from the flank gives +1 attack; from behind, +1 and the target's defense is halved. A unit on guard has neither flank nor rear. When you click on an enemy out of reach, your unit picks the best tile by itself.

Nodes (as in the original): each node radiates an aura as many tiles wide as its power. A Magic Spirit or Guardian Spirit that melds with it binds it to your magic: its aura then shimmers in your colors and brings you its power every turn (doubled by Node Mastery, and again by mastery of its realm). A battle fought on the node gives +2 attack, defense and resistance to the creatures of its realm, and often dispels spells from other realms (strength 50: a 10-mana spell has only a 17% chance of getting through); Node Mastery protects against this.
